```{python}
#| echo: false
import sys
sys.path.insert(0, "docs/assets")
from portal_helpers import load, fig_defaults, kpi_row, data_note, COLORS, blue_ramp
import plotly.graph_objects as go
import pandas as pd

data = load("mental_health")
```

The survey included a PHQ-4 proxy — a condensed four-item questionnaire capturing anxiety and
depression symptoms. Scores range from 0 (minimal distress) to 12 (severe distress).

---

::: {.section-header}
## Mean PHQ-4 score by age and gender
:::

```{python}
#| echo: false
mh_df = pd.DataFrame(data["mh_by_age_gender"])
age_groups = sorted(mh_df["age_group"].unique().tolist())

fig = go.Figure()
# Two blues, plus marker shape and line style, so the series don't rely on shade alone.
GENDER_STYLE = {
    "Man":   dict(color=blue_ramp(2)[0], symbol="circle",  dash="solid"),
    "Woman": dict(color=blue_ramp(2)[1], symbol="diamond", dash="dash"),
}
for gender, st in GENDER_STYLE.items():
    subset = mh_df[mh_df["gender"] == gender]
    vals   = []
    for ag in age_groups:
        row = subset[subset["age_group"] == ag]
        vals.append(float(row["mean_score"].values[0]) if len(row) else None)
    fig.add_trace(go.Scatter(
        x=age_groups, y=vals,
        mode="lines+markers",
        name=gender,
        line=dict(color=st["color"], width=2.5, dash=st["dash"]),
        marker=dict(size=9, symbol=st["symbol"], color=st["color"]),
        hovertemplate=f"{gender}: %{{y:.2f}}<extra></extra>",
    ))

# Reference lines for PHQ-4 severity thresholds
for y_val, label in [(3, "Mild (≥3)"), (6, "Moderate (≥6)")]:
    fig.add_hline(y=y_val, line_dash="dot", line_color=COLORS["muted"], line_width=1.5,
                  annotation_text=label, annotation_position="right")

fig.update_layout(yaxis_title="Mean PHQ-4 score (0–12)", xaxis_title="Age group")
fig_defaults(fig, "Mental Health Score by Age Group and Gender", height=400).show()
```

---

::: {.section-header}
## Depression and anxiety prevalence by age
*% reporting at least minimal symptoms*
:::

```{python}
#| echo: false
dep_anx = pd.DataFrame(data["dep_anx_by_age"])
ages = dep_anx["age_group"].tolist()

fig = go.Figure()
fig.add_trace(go.Bar(
    x=ages, y=dep_anx["pct_depression"],
    name="Depression", marker_color=blue_ramp(2)[0],
    hovertemplate="Depression: %{y:.1f}%<extra></extra>",
))
fig.add_trace(go.Bar(
    x=ages, y=dep_anx["pct_anxiety"],
    name="Anxiety", marker_color=blue_ramp(2)[1],
    hovertemplate="Anxiety: %{y:.1f}%<extra></extra>",
))
fig.update_layout(
    barmode="group",
    yaxis_title="Prevalence (%)",
    xaxis_title="Age group",
)
fig_defaults(fig, "Depression & Anxiety Prevalence by Age Group", height=400).show()
```

---

::: {.section-header}
## Correlations with other health measures
*Pearson r with 95% CI (pingouin)*
:::

```{python}
#| echo: false
corr_df = pd.DataFrame(data["correlations"])
# Focus on mental_health_score as Y variable
focus = corr_df[corr_df["Y"] == "mental_health_score"].copy()

var_labels = {
    "chronic_count": "# Chronic conditions",
    "er_visits_12mo": "ER visits (12 mo)",
    "bmi": "BMI",
}

fig = go.Figure()
for _, row in focus.iterrows():
    x_var  = row["X"]
    label  = var_labels.get(x_var, x_var)
    r_val  = row["r"]
    ci_lo, ci_hi = row["CI95%"]
    clr    = COLORS["primary"]
    fig.add_trace(go.Scatter(
        x=[r_val],
        y=[label],
        mode="markers",
        marker=dict(size=14, color=clr),
        error_x=dict(
            type="data",
            array=[ci_hi - r_val],
            arrayminus=[r_val - ci_lo],
            color=clr, thickness=2,
        ),
        name=label,
        hovertemplate=f"r = {r_val:.3f} [{ci_lo:.3f}, {ci_hi:.3f}]<extra>{label}</extra>",
    ))

fig.add_vline(x=0, line_dash="dash", line_color="#aaa", line_width=1)
fig.update_layout(
    xaxis_title="Pearson r (with 95% CI)",
    xaxis_range=[-0.5, 0.8],
    showlegend=False,
)
fig_defaults(fig, "Correlation with Mental Health Score (PHQ-4)", height=320).show()
```

::: {.stat-callout}
The strongest correlation with mental health distress is **number of chronic conditions** (r ≈ 0.5),
highlighting the bidirectional relationship between physical and mental health.
:::
